_note:
First cards for the Neutral pool ('Free Companies' per factions.json) and the Token sub-pool ('Summoned' -- cards that only ever enter play via another card's effect, never drafted/played from a starting deck). Neutral cards use faction:"neutral"; tokens use faction:"token" -- both already had entries in cards/factions.json (frame/crest/colors) but no cards existed for either until this session. NEU-prefixed ids for real Neutral pool cards, TOK-prefixed ids for tokens. art paths point at assets/art/neutral/ and assets/art/token/ respectively -- the token art folder does not exist on disk yet and will need to be created.

2026-08-17: expanded from 1 to 51 Neutral cards (NEU002-NEU051 added) to give the Neutral pool its intended role -- gap-filling for whichever faction's deck needs it, playable by either Ashborn or Verdant. Theme is deliberately 'the world outside the factions': city NPCs (guards, thieves, merchants, scholars), mundane/menagerie animals (guard dogs, pack mules, a chained bear -- captured/urban context, not Verdant's wild nature), and lost artifacts/constructs (automatons, sentinel statues, a colossus) -- nothing overlaps Ashborn's fire/dragon/sacrifice identity or Verdant's nature/Growth identity; Growth and Cleave were deliberately not used on any Neutral card to keep those signature to Verdant and Ashborn respectively. Composition was chosen from this session's balance-testing data: units 9 Attack / 9 Defense / 6 Support-unit, 16 Spells, 10 Support-duration (50 total) -- skewed harder toward spells/support-duration than either faction's own ~20%/10% split, on the reasoning that Neutral's job is to be a toolbox, and this session's simulator found both factions' utility slots (especially Ashborn's) underperform their unit slots -- see CLAUDE.md's balance-testing section. Rarity spread (31 Common / 12 Rare / 5 Epic / 2 Legendary) mirrors the ~62/23/10/5-scaled-to-50 spread used for both factions' 100-card sets. UnitType spread (14 Human / 6 Animal / 4 Construct) deliberately excludes Elemental and Dragon, which are Verdant's and Ashborn's respective signatures. Every rulesText clause reuses an existing template from the Ashborn/Verdant pool (verified against effects.py's dispatch tables) -- no new simulator code was needed to resolve any of the 50 new cards. Not yet re-balance-tested as an integrated 150-card pool beyond a crash-sweep + one 10,000-game sanity batch (see CLAUDE.md); numbers may need a follow-up pass once neutral cards see real play.
